messages.text: I’ll read the diff, calculate the required finding count, and check the changes for missing behavior and validation.
The diff includes extensive generated evidence. I’m focusing the review on the audit contract, backup safety, and whether the new verification scripts prove their stated guarantees.

I reproduced two backup safety gaps: pre-existing destination sidecars can be deleted, and an interrupted backup leaves a visible zero-byte output. I also confirmed malformed audit facts can pass validation and date-only queries require a full scan and sort.

- Finding floor: 4,850,551 bytes ÷ 1,000 = 4,850.551 kB; N = min(⌊√4,850.551 + 1⌋, 10) = min(70, 10) = **10**.
- [backup_db.py:18](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/scripts/backup_db.py:18): Check destination sidecars before opening SQLite. An absent destination main file can still have existing `-wal`, `-shm`, or `-journal` files. I reproduced a successful backup deleting pre-existing `-wal` and `-journal` files; the failure cleanup also unconditionally deletes these paths. Reject namespace collisions and clean up only files created by this invocation.
- [backup_db.py:18](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/scripts/backup_db.py:18): The final backup filename becomes visible before any copying or validation. Terminating a blocked backup left a zero-byte destination, and a subsequent attempt refuses to overwrite it. Write to a private staging file and publish the final filename only after successful validation, preserving the no-overwrite guarantee.
- [backup_db.py:23](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/scripts/backup_db.py:23): `origin.backup(target)` has no operation deadline. SQLite backup retries busy/locked sources beyond the connection timeout; an exclusive-lock reproduction remained blocked after six seconds. Add a bounded deadline through the backup progress callback and test cleanup after timeout.
- [backup_db.py:24](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/scripts/backup_db.py:24): The reported checks do not establish that the backup contains this application’s database. An existing zero-byte source returns success, `integrity_check=["ok"]`, and `schema_version=0`. Validate the expected application schema, or explicitly distinguish a structurally valid SQLite copy from an application-compatible recovery backup.
- [dto.py:20](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/booking_app/dto.py:20): Snapshot validation accepts contradictory audit facts. I reproduced `room.updated` with `before=null`, `target_id=1`, `after.id=999`, and `capacity=-1` returning successfully. Validate action/type agreement, creation versus transition before-values, snapshot identity, and domain invariants so corrupted evidence produces the documented safe error.
- [audit.js:23](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/booking_app/static/audit.js:23): Frontend snapshot validation checks property names without checking their values. A response containing `after.name={password:"secret"}` or a string capacity passes `eventShape` and is rendered as valid evidence. Validate snapshot field types and nullable fields, and add malformed-value cases to the handler tests.
- [services.py:123](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/booking_app/services.py:123): The existing index begins with `target_type`, leaving default and date-only audit queries without an appropriate chronological index. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows both `SCAN audit_events` and `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`. Add an `(occurred_at, id)` index and verify the date-only query plan; these queries otherwise scan and sort the entire growing history.
- [audit.js:79](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/booking_app/static/audit.js:79): Loaded results do not identify the filters that produced them. After querying bookings, changing the selector to rooms leaves booking results under the new selection with only a record-count message. Preserve and display the submitted filters, or mark results stale when inputs change.
- [verify_audit_browser.py:43](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/scripts/verify_audit_browser.py:43): The browser runner defaults to a machine-specific macOS Chrome path. The documented command fails on Linux and on machines with Playwright Chromium installed but no Chrome at that location, despite the README saying browser setup follows the existing portable runners. Resolve Playwright’s installed Chromium when no explicit executable is supplied.
- [verify_audit_browser.cjs:17](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/scripts/verify_audit_browser.cjs:17): The browser’s `exact_dto` and complete-evidence claims are stronger than its assertions. It checks response keys, row counts, and an expansion label, but never compares rendered actor/action/target/time/reason or expanded before/after values against the response. Add those DOM comparisons, including a cancellation and revocation, so omitted or incorrectly bound evidence fields cannot still produce PASS.
